fields.meta_description: Build a training feedback form that rates each module, alerts trainers to gaps and checks 30 days later whether the course stuck.
fields.h1: Build a Training Feedback Form That Follows Up
fields.hero_description: Describe the course and what it should change. Emergent builds the training feedback form, sends it as the session ends, and checks back once people are working again.
fields.features_heading: Everything That Happens After the Last Slide
fields.features_subheading: Most templates stop at a page of rating scales. These six pieces connect each answer to a person and a next step.
fields.feature_1:
A rating for every module of the course

Ask trainees to rate each module on its own scale, with a comment box under any low score. The trainer sees which hour of the day lost the room instead of one blended average.
fields.feature_2:
Answers linked to the trainee's record

Prefill the trainee's name, the course, and the session date from the invite link. Every response lands on that person's training record, beside the courses they finished before.
fields.feature_3:
A follow-up form a month later

Send a shorter form a few weeks after the course to ask whether the skill is in use. Their manager gets the same question, and both answers sit next to the scores from the day.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a trainee is not ready

Message the trainer in Slack or by email when someone marks a module as not confident. The alert names the trainee and the module, and the trainer books a refresher before sign-off.
fields.feature_5:
Results grouped by trainer and cohort

Filter every answer by the trainer who taught it or the cohort that took it. Put the spring cohort next to the fall one, or compare two trainers who teach the same course.
fields.feature_6:
The full codebase in your own repo

Export the whole app to your GitHub on paid plans when training records have to live inside your HR systems. Your engineers host it and change it like any other internal tool.
fields.why_title: Why Use Emergent for Training Feedback?
fields.why_description: A paper evaluation sheet is filled in while people pack up, then filed. Nobody asks a month later whether anything changed.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Trainings That Act on the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
One shaky answer on load checks books a refresher

Brightwater Distribution runs a forklift refresher every spring. Before sign-off, each operator rates their confidence on every module. Chris Walker marked load stability as not confident. The trainer got a message, and a hands-on session with Chris went on the calendar for Thursday.
fields.tab_content_2:
Which accounts can build approval rules alone

Larkline Software trains each new customer's admins live. The feedback form ends on one question: could you build an approval rule alone today? Answers roll up by account. Harbor Dental Group had 1 of 4 admins ready, and Priya Nair, its success manager, got a message to book a second session.
fields.tab_content_3:
Thirty days later, who still uses the checklist

Pinecrest Credit Union taught 18 tellers a fraud-spotting course, which scored 4.6 out of 5 on the day itself. A second form 30 days later asked each teller whether they had used the check fraud checklist at the window. Eleven of the 18 had. Their branch managers got the same question.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three seats held on a 2 out of 5 verdict

Tern Engineering pays for outside courses and asks for feedback afterward. Owen Park took a $1,450 structural modeling course. On his phone, he rated it 2 out of 5 on whether he would send a colleague. Three seats booked for the next cohort went on hold, and Lucia Ferraro, the learning manager, got his comments.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Training Feedback Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what the course was supposed to change before you write a single question.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask how they will use it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one line on what trainees should do differently after the course, such as running a pre-use forklift check unprompted. Every question on the form should help you learn whether that happened. Questions that cannot inform a decision about the course can go.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give every module its own rating on one five-point scale, and label both ends in plain words. A single overall score hides the weak hour. Add a required comment box that opens under any rating of 2 or lower.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Close with two open questions: what the trainee will try first at work, and what was missing. These answers tell the trainer more than any average. They also give the follow-up form something specific to ask about later.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put a QR code on the last slide and leave 10 minutes for the form. Response rates drop once people are back at their desks. For remote sessions, drop the link in the chat while everyone is still on the call.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the course, the modules, the trainers, and who should hear about a low score. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a results dashboard. Change a question later by asking for it in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set a shorter form to reach the trainee and their manager about a month after the course. Ask whether they have used it and what got in the way. Line those answers up against the scores from the day.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Take it yourself on a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone, as a trainee would, and time it. Mark one module as low and check that the comment box opens and the trainer gets the alert. Delete the test response before the session.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is two Scribd PDFs, a Quenza listicle, template pages from Visme, involve.me and Cloud Assess, an Emitrr PDF and a UK charity's evaluation form, with Jotform holding the AI Overview. Each one is a list of rating questions that ends when the session ends. None ties an answer to the trainee, the customer account or the course fee, and none asks again weeks later whether the skill is in use. This page answers the People Also Ask questions on what to ask and how to word it, then shows four trainings where the answers drive a next step: a forklift refresher booked for one operator, a customer account flagged to its success manager, a 30-day check on whether a course changed the work, and a paid outside course judged before more seats are bought.
tab_stories: After a forklift refresher at Brightwater Distribution, each operator rates their confidence on every module, and Chris Walker's not-confident answer on load stability books him a hands-on session with the trainer before his sign-off.

Larkline Software trains each new customer's admins on a live session, and the feedback per account shows Harbor Dental Group with 1 of 4 admins ready to build approval rules alone, so its success manager gets a message.

Pinecrest Credit Union sends tellers a second form 30 days after a fraud-spotting course, asking whether they have used the checklist on the job, and puts that answer beside the 4.6 the course scored on the day.

Tern Engineering paid $1,450 for an engineer's outside course, and his phone answer of 2 out of 5 on whether he would send a colleague puts the 3 seats booked for the next cohort on hold for the learning manager.

claims_to_source: The Kirkpatrick model evaluates training at four levels: reaction, learning, behavior and results
Level 1, reaction, captures whether participants found the training engaging and relevant to their job
Level 3, behavior, measures whether people apply what they learned back on the job
